literal: Later he served as Left Assistant Director of the Shouyang Route Office and was captured together with Wang Lin and the others.
idiomatic: Later he became left assistant director on the Shouyang route staff and was taken prisoner along with Wang Lin and his companions.

literal: At the end of the Zhou dynasty he escaped and returned.
idiomatic: When the Zhou dynasty drew to its close, he broke free and made his way home.

literal: In the early Kaihuang era he was Administrator of Yong'an.
idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang reign he served as prefect of Yong'an.

literal: He died while serving as Chief Administrator of Jiang Province.
idiomatic: He died in office as chief administrator of Jiang Province.

literal: His son Zhengzao was bright, quick-witted, and capable.
idiomatic: His son Zhengzao was quick-minded and gifted with real capacity.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was a Palace Corps military attendant with honorary general's retinue rank, adjudicating Secretarial Archive affairs.
idiomatic: Near the end of Wuping he held the rank of palace-corps military attendant with an opening-establishment commission and supervised the secretarial archive.

literal: Because his father Taotuo had died in Chen captivity, Zhengzao immediately pleaded illness and resigned his office; grief wore him to the bone, and in dwelling, conduct, and meals he kept to the rites of mourning — men of worth praised him.
idiomatic: When his father Taotuo perished in Chen captivity, Zhengzao at once pleaded illness and quit his post. Grief wore him thin; in how he lived, moved, and ate he kept to mourning rites as though the coffin still stood in the hall — and men of judgment praised him for it.

literal: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he served in succession as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works within the Masters of Writing and as magistrate of Zhouzhi County.
idiomatic: Under the Sui, during Kaihuang, he served in turn as outer gentleman in the works bureau of the masters of writing and as magistrate of Zhouzhi.

literal: He died while serving as Chief Administrator of Yi Province.
idiomatic: He died in office as chief administrator of Yi Province.

literal: Taotuo's younger brother Wenshi was Attendant Drafting Master of the Palace Secretariat and Administrator of Qi Commandery.
idiomatic: Taotuo's younger brother Wenshi was drafting master of the palace secretariat and prefect of Qi Commandery.

literal: Of Yishen's seven brothers, many had scholarly interests.
idiomatic: Among Yishen's seven brothers, many pursued learning.

literal: The second brother, Tonggui, was known for Confucian learning.
idiomatic: The second brother, Tonggui, won renown for Confucian scholarship.

literal: The sixth brother, Zhilian, has his own biography.
idiomatic: The sixth brother, Zhilian, is treated in a separate biography.

literal: Yishen's clansman Shenwei.
idiomatic: Yishen's clansman Shenwei.

literal: His great-grandfather Rong had been Attendant Master of Writing under Wei; Shenwei from youth showed moral bearing, inherited the family tradition, and had a rough grasp of ritual learning and moral principles.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong had been attendant master of writing under Wei. Shenwei showed moral force even as a boy, carried on the family tradition, and had a working knowledge of ritual and moral teaching.

literal: He also loved music and compiled a Book of Music amounting to nearly a hundred scrolls.
idiomatic: He also loved music and compiled a Book of Music running to nearly a hundred scrolls.

literal: At the end of Eastern Wei he was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the final years of Eastern Wei he was left vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: He died at the start of Tianbao.
idiomatic: He died at the opening of the Tianbao reign.

literal: Posthumously granted Governor of Xin Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Xin Province.

literal: The historian writes: Yuanzhong came from an ordinary lineage, known for learning and moral teaching; his repute in human relations was never one that credited him with the arts of stratagem and alliance.
idiomatic: The historian writes: Yuanzhong sprang from a plain family, known for learning and moral teaching — a man whose name in human affairs was never linked to the arts of alliance and intrigue.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang died in mysterious circumstances and the barbarian clique seized power unlawfully, every man of ambition looked for a royal rescue army.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang died in shadow and the barbarian faction seized unlawful power, every man of will and talent turned his eyes toward a king's army marching to restore the throne.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor turned his chariot east, purpose and heart aligned; upon meeting that heroic figure he poured out his liver and gall — a stone cast into water, sure to sink without trace. Was that mere chance?
idiomatic: When Gao Huan turned his chariot east, wish and circumstance met as one; at the first sight of that heroic bearing Yuanzhong poured out his whole heart — a stone thrown into water, bound to sink to the bottom. Could that have been accident alone?

literal: Having tasted merit and fame, he finally knew when to halt and be content — in the way he advanced and retreated, there is something worth observing.
idiomatic: Having tasted merit and fame, he learned at last where to stop and be satisfied — in how he came forward and stepped back, there is a lesson worth keeping.

literal: Wenwei bore noble prestige and radiant lineage; early he had high aspirations. Through hardship and peril he at last met a hero-lord; though rank and honors were never lavish, he still counts among those who helped establish the realm.
idiomatic: Wenwei carried weight of birth and bright lineage, and early held high purpose. Through straits and dangers he at last found a lord of heroic stamp; though rank and reward never ran deep, he still belongs among those who helped seat the throne.

literal: Xunzu's literary style blazed with ornament and he won fame early; riding the strength of talent and birth, he gave free rein to pride and affectation — in the capital, none did not fear the edge of his tongue.
idiomatic: Xunzu's writing flared with color and he won a name while still young; trusting in talent and station, he indulged pride and display — in the capital, everyone feared the cut of his tongue.

literal: His appointments never rose to great notice; he died young. Had he lived to full white-browed age, who could measure how far he might have risen or fallen?
idiomatic: Preferment never truly found him; he died in early manhood. Had he lived to frost his brows with age, who could say what heights or depths awaited him?

literal: The encomium says: Jinyang and Daxia — holding substance, embracing culture.
idiomatic: The encomium says: Jinyang and Daxia — men who held to substance and carried culture in their hearts.

literal: Walking in benevolence, treading in righteousness, all met the turning of the age.
idiomatic: They walked in benevolence and stood in righteousness, and all alike caught the storm when the age turned.

literal: Lu nurtured commerce and gain; Li disdained the clamor of the times.
idiomatic: Lu turned his hand to trade and profit; Li turned his face from the noise of a corrupt age.

literal: Constancy from first to last — here the pure and the turbid divide.
idiomatic: Constancy from beginning to end — here the clear and the muddy part ways.

literal: Yishen served as counselor and aide, yet fell short of devoted loyalty.
idiomatic: Yishen lent counsel and support, yet fell short of steadfast loyalty.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
